newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Perm joins Russian regional Eurobond queue.
newsitem.headline: Perm joins Russian regional Eurobond queue.

text.p: Russia's Urals region of Perm, said on Tuesday it planned to join a long line of regions tapping international capital markets with a Eurobond.

First Deputy Governor Yuri Belousov, speaking as the City of Moscow launched a tightly priced $500 million Eurobond in London, told Reuters by telephone from Perm the region planned to raise between $50 and $200 million through a Eurobond.
Many other Russian regions, including Tatarstan republic, and the Siberian region of Irkutsk, have announced plans to issue Eurobonds.
A March presidential decree mandated the City of Moscow, St Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod region to issue Eurobonds.
The City of Moscow opened the regional Eurobond invasion on Tuesday by offering its three-year Eurobond at a spread of 315 basis points.
St Petersburg started a road-show for its paper on Friday.
Nizhny Novgorod said it would submit its issue prospectus to the Finance Ministry by the end of May or in early June.
Belousov said Perm had already had talks with ING-Barings and Russia's Inkombank on organising ratings.
"There were not just preliminary talks," he said. "These banks propose organising the whole issue."
But he said the administration would set up a tender for lead-manager next week.
Belousov said Perm had received nine billion roubles ($1.5 million) this year of federal funding.
A draft law on regional Eurobonds says regions receiving funding from the federal government cannot issue Eurobonds.
But Belousov said this small amount of funding would not hurt the issue plans.
"We do not think there will be any special problems with that," he said.
Belousov said the volume of the issue would depend on the rating. "It may vary, but it will mainly depend on the rating," he said.
St Petersburg plans to raise up to $300 million and Nizhny Novgorod up to $100 million.
Belousov said the economic situation in Perm made him expect a rating no worse than Nizhny Novgorod's.
Moody's assigned Nizhny Novgorod Ba2 and Standard & Poor's BB-, the same ratings as on Russia's sovereign Eurobonds.

Russia raised $1 billion through a debut Eurobond in November and two billion marks ($1.2 billion) in March. In June it plans to issue another dollar Eurobond and the Finance Ministry said the volume would be comparable to the first two issues.
Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin told a meeting of senior Finance Ministry officials on Tuesday that Russia should consider issuing more frequent, but smaller Eurobonds.
--Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520 ($ = 1.693 German Marks)
